privacy.metaDescription: Privacy policy for Naver Blog Image Downloader — what data this project collects, how it is used, and your rights.
privacy.intro: "Naver Blog Image Downloader" is an open-source personal project that operates under a minimum-data-collection principle. No account is required; this project does not sell data and does not serve ads. This page explains what the project collects, how it is used, and how you can exercise control.

sections.title: What this project collects
body: Naver Blog URLs you submit: sent from the Web app to the project's backend service solely to fetch and package images, and not used further once processing completes. The project does not actively persist submitted URLs to long-term storage; cloud infrastructure (AWS) system logs may briefly retain related technical traces and are rotated per AWS defaults.

Local data (not uploaded): your locale, theme preference, and whether you have dismissed the onboarding card are stored only in your browser's Local Storage, are never sent to any server, and can be cleared at any time from your browser settings.

sections.title: How the project uses data
body: To deliver the core feature — fetching, packaging, and downloading Naver Blog images.
The project explicitly does not: profile users, serve ads, sell data, or track users across websites.
The project does not use any collected data for AI model training. How third-party services may process data on their own side is subject to their respective privacy policies.

sections.title: Third-party services
body: AWS Lambda + S3 (Amazon Web Services, Inc.): backend packaging pipeline and transient ZIP storage, operated by the project maintainer.

Naver: the URLs you provide point to Naver Blog. You are responsible for ensuring your use complies with Naver's Terms of Service. The project provides a technical tool only; it does not endorse any particular use and has no commercial or licensing relationship with Naver.

sections.title: Cross-border data transfers
body: The backend packaging pipeline runs in an AWS region chosen by the project maintainer. Beyond that, the project does not transfer user data to any other region or third party.

For users located in the EU/EEA, such cross-border transfers rely on the Standard Contractual Clauses (SCC) published by Amazon Web Services as the appropriate safeguard under GDPR Article 46; for other users, continued use of this product indicates awareness of the above transfers.

sections.title: Retention and deletion
body: Packaged ZIP files in S3: automatically deleted 1 day after creation via a bucket lifecycle rule on the "jobs/" prefix.
Download links (presigned URLs): valid for 1 hour, expiring automatically thereafter.
Local data: cleared by removing this site's Local Storage through your browser settings. The project cannot and does not access this data remotely.
If the project is discontinued, any remaining temporary files in S3 will be deleted as part of the shutdown process.

sections.title: Security
body: All traffic between the Web app and backend services is encrypted via HTTPS/TLS. Cloud storage (AWS S3) encrypts data at rest per platform defaults. The project does not export data to any third party not disclosed in this policy.

If a security incident involving personal data occurs, the project will announce it on GitHub Release Notes within a reasonable time, and will notify the relevant supervisory authority and any affected users the project can identify within the time required by applicable law (for example, within 72 hours under GDPR Article 33, or within 24 hours under South Korea's PIPA §34).

sections.title: Your rights
body: There is no account system and no "log out" concept. To stop using the product, simply close the site.
You can clear this site's Local Storage through your browser settings, removing your locale, theme preference, and onboarding state.

Because the project does not collect data sufficient to identify an individual user, the access, rectification, portability, objection, and individual-erasure rights under GDPR Articles 15–20 cannot be fulfilled on a per-user basis by the project. If you are located in the EU/EEA and have a specific concern, please reach out via the channel below; the project will respond within a reasonable time (within 30 days per GDPR standards) and will explain if a request cannot be executed due to technical limitations.

sections.title: Children's privacy
body: This product is not designed for children and does not knowingly collect data from them. Jurisdictions define "child" differently (13 under US COPPA, 14 under South Korea's PIPA, 16 under EU GDPR — reducible to 13 by member states). The project does not knowingly collect data from anyone in these categories.

Because the project does not collect data sufficient to identify an individual user, it cannot identify or delete a specific child's records on a per-user basis. If a particular collection method is found to risk inadvertent collection from children, the project will immediately stop that method. Any temporary files remaining in S3 are still deleted at shutdown per "Retention and deletion".

sections.title: Legal basis and scope
body: This policy applies to users worldwide. If you are located in the European Union or EEA, the project relies on GDPR Article 6(1)(b) — performance of the service contract between you and the project — as the legal basis for processing the Blog URLs you submit.

If you are a California resident, you are entitled under the CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act) to rights including the right to know, the right to delete, and the right to non-discrimination. The project does not sell or share personal data, so it does not provide a "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information" button; you may exercise the above rights via the contact channel below.
Where other jurisdictions impose mandatory rules (such as South Korea's PIPA or other US state laws), the project complies within their scope.

sections.title: Policy changes
body: The "Last updated" date on this page is authoritative. Material changes will be announced in advance via GitHub Release Notes; continued use of the product after the announcement constitutes acceptance of the updated version.
